quests.instruction: Our team plays ___ the Blue Eagles on Saturday, and the match starts at ten. Which word belongs here?
quests.hint: The Blue Eagles are the other team, the opponents.
quests.explanation: 'Against' shows an opponent: play against, race against, compete against. 'With' would mean they are on the same team.
quests.funFact: In sports results, 'vs' is short for 'versus', which means 'against'.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about practice is written correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: We train on Tuesdays, at six o'clock, in the sports hall.
options: We train in Tuesdays, on six o'clock, at the sports hall.
We train on Tuesdays, at six o'clock, in the sports hall.
We train at Tuesdays, in six o'clock, on the sports hall.
quests.hint: Look for a day, a clock time and a room.
quests.explanation: 'On Tuesdays' uses 'on' for days, 'at six o'clock' uses 'at' for a clock time, and 'in the sports hall' uses 'in' for an indoor space. The others swap them.
quests.funFact: Sports halls have lines marked on the floor for different games.

quests.instruction: Zara kicked the ball ___ the goalkeeper's hands and into the net. Which word is missing?
quests.hint: The ball goes by the keeper's hands without being stopped.
quests.explanation: 'Past' shows movement that goes by something. The ball goes past the keeper's hands. 'Under' would put it below them.
quests.funFact: A goal counts when the whole ball crosses the goal line.

quests.instruction: In hide-and-seek, Leo counts ___ twenty with his eyes closed while the others hide. Which word fits?
quests.hint: He counts up from one until he reaches the number.
quests.explanation: 'Count to twenty' shows the number we count up to. 'At twenty' and 'in twenty' do not fit.
quests.funFact: Hide-and-seek is played in many countries under different names.

quests.instruction: Sam has won every game ___ chess this month. Which preposition fits?
quests.hint: We name which game it is.
quests.explanation: 'A game of chess' names the kind of game: a game of cards, a game of football.
quests.funFact: A chess board has sixty-four squares.

quests.instruction: The treasure in our game is hidden ___ the sofa and the bookcase. Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: Two things are named after the blank.
quests.explanation: 'Between' is used for two things: the sofa and the bookcase. 'Among' would need a group of three or more.
quests.funFact: In treasure-hunt games, clues often name two landmarks.

quests.instruction: Hana is crazy ___ drawing animals, and she fills a page every day. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We use this word to say what someone loves very much.
quests.explanation: 'Crazy about' means loving something very much. 'Crazy at' and 'crazy of' are not used here.
quests.funFact: 'Mad about' and 'wild about' mean the same as 'crazy about'.

quests.instruction: Raj collects stamps ___ all over the world. Which word fits?
quests.hint: Many different countries are the sources of the stamps.
quests.explanation: 'From all over the world' shows the places the stamps come from.
quests.funFact: Stamp collecting is called philately.

quests.instruction: Layla plays the violin ___ the school orchestra. Which word fits?
quests.hint: She is a member of the group.
quests.explanation: 'In the orchestra' means as a member of the group. 'By' and 'to' do not give this meaning.
quests.funFact: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play together.

quests.instruction: Dad usually tidies the kitchen ___ dinner, when everyone has finished eating. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: Everyone has finished eating first.
quests.explanation: Tidying happens when everyone has finished eating, which is later than dinner, so Dad tidies after dinner.
quests.funFact: In many homes, family members take turns to wash up.

quests.instruction: We take our shoes off ___ the door and leave them on the mat. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: The door is a point where we enter.
quests.explanation: 'At the door' names the place where we do something. 'On the door' would mean on its surface.
quests.funFact: In many countries, people take their shoes off at the door.

quests.instruction: Please finish your homework ___ bedtime, so you can read a story. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The homework must be done no later than bedtime.
quests.explanation: 'By bedtime' is a deadline: no later than that time. 'Until bedtime' would mean working all the way up to it.
quests.funFact: Many families have a regular bedtime routine.

quests.instruction: Ravi left his lunchbox ___ the bus, and now he has no lunch. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: Think about large public vehicles.
quests.explanation: We say 'on the bus', 'on the train' and 'on a plane' for public transport. 'In the bus' is less natural.
quests.funFact: Lost property offices keep things that people leave on buses and trains.

quests.instruction: Ali is late ___ school because his bus broke down. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: We say 'late' plus the event or the place we should be at.
quests.explanation: 'Late for' plus an event or a place: late for school, late for work. 'Late at' and 'late of' are not used.
quests.funFact: 'Late' and 'later' are different words: 'later' means after some time.

quests.instruction: My lost book has been found under the teacher's desk, between the bin and the wall. Which sentence is correct?
quests.correctAnswer: It is under the teacher's desk, between the bin and the wall.
options: It is on the teacher's desk, among the bin and the wall.
It is under the teacher's desk, between of the bin and the wall.
It is under the teacher's desk, between the bin and the wall.
quests.hint: Check 'under', 'between' and what comes after it.
quests.explanation: 'Under the desk' shows below it, and 'between the bin and the wall' names two things. The others change a word or add 'of'.
quests.funFact: A bin is often kept near a teacher's desk.

quests.instruction: Dad can't hear the TV ___ the noise of the washing machine. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The loud noise covers the quiet sound.
quests.explanation: 'Over the noise' means with a loud noise covering the sound, so he can't hear the TV. 'Past' shows movement.
quests.funFact: We often say 'speak over the noise' when a place is loud.

quests.instruction: Mum is baking a cake ___ Grandpa's birthday, which is next Sunday. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The cake celebrates an occasion.
quests.explanation: 'For' shows the purpose or occasion of something: a cake for his birthday. 'At' and 'to' do not give this meaning.
quests.funFact: Birthday cakes with candles are popular in many countries.

quests.instruction: The baby fell asleep ___ the car ride, so we did not wake her when we got home. Which word completes the sentence?
quests.hint: The word needs a noun after it, not a verb.
quests.explanation: 'During the car ride' is correct because 'during' is followed by a noun phrase. 'While' needs a clause with a verb.
quests.funFact: Babies often fall asleep in cars because of the gentle movement.

quests.instruction: Everything is ___ sale this week, with prices cut by half. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The prices are lower than usual.
quests.explanation: 'On sale' means sold at a lower price. 'For sale' means that something can be bought.
quests.funFact: 'Sale' is also the name for a time when shops lower their prices.

quests.instruction: The house next door is ___ sale; there is a sign in the garden. Which word fits?
quests.hint: A sign shows that anyone can buy it.
quests.explanation: 'For sale' means that something is available to buy. 'On sale' usually means sold at a lower price.
quests.funFact: 'For sale' signs often show a phone number.

quests.instruction: The toy is ___ stock, so you can take one home today. Which word fits?
quests.hint: The shop has it ready to sell.
quests.explanation: 'In stock' means that the shop has the item available. The opposite is 'out of stock'.
quests.funFact: Shops count their stock so they know what to order.

quests.instruction: Take the second road ___ the left, just after the post office. Which word completes the sentence?
quests.hint: Directions use this word with 'left' and 'right'.
quests.explanation: We say 'on the left' and 'on the right' for directions. 'At the left' and 'in the left' are not used this way.
quests.funFact: A map can help people who find left and right confusing.

quests.instruction: Keep walking ___ the end of the street, and then turn right. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: You walk all the way and reach the end.
quests.explanation: 'Walk to the end of' shows where we travel until we arrive. 'At the end of' describes a place, not a walk.
quests.funFact: A street with no way through is called a dead end.

quests.instruction: The old bridge goes ___ the river and leads to the town on the other side. Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: It links one bank to the other.
quests.explanation: 'Across' shows movement or position from one side of something to the other. The bridge links the two banks.
quests.funFact: Some bridges are built high so that boats can pass beneath them.

quests.instruction: 'Why are you wet?' 'I walked home ___ the rain without an umbrella.' Choose the missing word.
quests.hint: You are outside, with the rain all around you.
quests.explanation: 'In the rain' means while it is raining and we are out in it. 'Under the rain' is not used.
quests.funFact: 'In the rain' and 'in the snow' are common English phrases.

quests.instruction: 'What's the matter ___ Tom?' 'He lost his dog.' Which word fits?
quests.hint: This is a fixed question.
quests.explanation: 'What's the matter with ...?' is a fixed question for asking why someone looks upset. 'For' and 'at' do not fit.
quests.funFact: 'What's wrong with you?' means the same but can sound unfriendly.

quests.instruction: 'How do I get to the swimming pool?' Which reply sounds natural?
quests.correctAnswer: Go along this road, past the school, and it is on your right.
options: Go through this road, by the school, and it is at your right.
Go along this road, past the school, and it is on your right.
Go across this road, over the school, and it is in your right.
quests.hint: Check the road, the school and the right.
quests.explanation: 'Along this road', 'past the school' and 'on your right' are the natural patterns for directions. The other replies use the wrong small words.
quests.funFact: Giving directions is easier when you name a building people can see.

quests.instruction: Which sentence describes the walk correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: After school, we walk through the park, along the river and past the library.
options: Before school, we walk across the park, through the river and past of the library.
After school, we walk through the park, along the river and past the library.
After school, we walk beside the park, over the river and between the library.
quests.hint: Think about the order of the day and each movement.
quests.explanation: 'Through the park', 'along the river' and 'past the library' describe three natural movements. The other sentences use words that do not fit, like 'through the river'.
quests.funFact: A good description of a journey uses a different small word for each part.

quests.instruction: 'How long is the film?' 'It runs ___ half past six until nine.' Which word makes the sentence correct?
quests.hint: She gives both the start and the end.
quests.explanation: 'From half past six until nine' gives the start and the end of the film. 'At' and 'by' only give one time.
quests.funFact: Films are often described by their running time.

quests.instruction: Mia is worried ___ the long flight, but her dad will sit next to her. Which word fits?
quests.hint: We name the thing that makes her feel anxious.
quests.explanation: 'Worried about' plus the thing that causes the worry. 'Worried of' and 'worried at' are not used.
quests.funFact: Many airlines have special help for nervous flyers.
